answer: A ferrous anchor makes Sybil attacks expensive: bind each agent identity to a hardware attestation key burned into one physical device, plus a refundable stake deposit. An orchard of fake identities then needs one real device and one locked deposit per clone, so the attacker pays linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation earned by one identity cannot echo across clones, so a Sybil farm gains no free trust and any misbehaviour slashes only the deposit of the offending identity.
